case_name: In Re APPLICATION OF ENBRIDGE ENERGY TO REPLACE AND RELOCATE LINE 5

issues.label: PSC statutory jurisdiction
issues.why: Court must confirm PSC had legal authority to approve this pipeline replacement under Michigan statutes.

issues.label: Applicable approval standard
issues.why: Court must identify the correct legal test (e.g., public convenience/necessity, reasonableness, safety) governing PSC approval.

issues.label: Scope of PSC review
issues.why: Court must decide whether PSC properly limited or expanded its review to pipeline construction versus broader policy/environmental concerns.

issues.label: Standard of judicial review
issues.why: Court must apply the correct deference and review standards to PSC fact-finding, legal conclusions, and discretionary choices.

issues.label: Preservation and exhaustion
issues.why: Court must determine whether appellants preserved issues and exhausted administrative remedies before judicial review.

issues.label: Standing of each appellant
issues.why: Court must verify each appellant (including Tribes) has standing under Michigan law to challenge PSC approval.

issues.label: Tribal standing and injury
issues.why: Court must assess whether asserted treaty, cultural, fishing, or resource injuries satisfy standing requirements.

issues.label: Ripeness and finality
issues.why: Court must decide whether PSC action is final and the dispute is ripe given other permits, easements, and future contingencies.

issues.label: Mootness and changed circumstances
issues.why: Court must consider whether later events or approvals render any claims moot or alter the controversy.

issues.label: Proper parties and intervention
issues.why: Court must confirm necessary parties were included and intervention/participation rights were correctly handled.

issues.label: Due process in PSC proceedings
issues.why: Court must assess whether notice, opportunity to be heard, evidentiary rights, and impartiality were adequate.

issues.label: Administrative record completeness
issues.why: Court must ensure review is confined to and supported by the certified record and that record disputes are resolved correctly.

issues.label: Burden of proof allocation
issues.why: Court must confirm PSC placed the burden on Enbridge (and on challengers where applicable) under the governing statutes.

issues.label: Substantial evidence support
issues.why: Court must determine whether key PSC findings (need, safety, alternatives) are supported by substantial evidence.

issues.label: Arbitrary or capricious action
issues.why: Court must decide whether PSC’s approval was irrational, inconsistent, or an abuse of discretion.

issues.label: Consistency with prior PSC approvals
issues.why: Court must consider how the 1953 PSC approval and subsequent history affect current authority and analysis.

issues.label: Collateral attack doctrine
issues.why: Court must determine whether challenges impermissibly re-litigate or undermine the 1953 approval affirmed in Lakehead v Dehn.

issues.label: Effect of 1963 Constitution art 4 §52
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether constitutional environmental-protection duties constrain or inform PSC decisionmaking.

issues.label: MEPA applicability to PSC action
issues.why: Court must decide whether MEPA applies to PSC approvals and what duties it imposes (feasible alternatives, prudent measures).

issues.label: MEPA cause of action viability
issues.why: Court must determine whether appellants can raise MEPA claims in this posture and against these defendants.

issues.label: MEPA standard of review
issues.why: Court must apply MEPA’s substantive tests rather than only administrative-law deference where required.

issues.label: Definition of natural resources
issues.why: Court must assess whether the Great Lakes/Straits impacts fall within protected resources under MEPA/NREPA.

issues.label: Risk-of-spill evaluation
issues.why: Court must decide whether PSC adequately evaluated spill probability/severity from existing lines versus replacement.

issues.label: Comparative environmental impacts
issues.why: Court must determine whether PSC properly compared impacts of the tunnel project with continued operation of dual pipes.

issues.label: Need and public benefit
issues.why: Court must assess whether evidence supports a finding of public need/benefit, including Michigan-specific benefits.

issues.label: Primarily out-of-state service
issues.why: Court must consider whether predominantly serving Canada undermines statutory criteria for approval in Michigan.

issues.label: Energy security considerations
issues.why: Court must address evidence about propane supply, jet fuel, and in-state facilities dependent on Line 5.

issues.label: Alternatives analysis
issues.why: Court must determine whether PSC considered feasible and prudent alternatives (shutdown, reroute, rail/truck, other fuels).

issues.label: No-change-in-capacity significance
issues.why: Court must decide how maintaining capacity affects need, risk, and statutory criteria.

issues.label: Safety regulation scope
issues.why: Court must determine PSC’s role versus federal pipeline safety regulators and preemption boundaries.

issues.label: Federal preemption
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether federal law preempts state conditions or review of pipeline safety/design/operation.

issues.label: Interstate and international commerce
issues.why: Court must consider Commerce Clause/foreign affairs constraints on state actions affecting cross-border pipelines.

issues.label: Treaty rights adjudication
issues.why: Court must decide whether and how state approval can proceed without unlawfully impairing treaty fishing rights.

issues.label: Tribal consultation requirements
issues.why: Court must evaluate any statutory, constitutional, or common-law duties to consult Tribes in the approval process.

issues.label: Cultural resources impacts
issues.why: Court must determine whether impacts on cultural, subsistence, or spiritual interests were legally required to be considered.

issues.label: Public trust doctrine relevance
issues.why: Court must consider whether Great Lakes/Straits implicate public trust duties affecting state approvals and easements.

issues.label: State’s submerged lands authority
issues.why: Court must assess legality of state-granted easements/leases under the Straits and their interaction with PSC approval.

issues.label: Validity of MSCA framework
issues.why: Court must determine whether 2018 PA 359 and MSCA actions lawfully authorize the tunnel and related property arrangements.

issues.label: DNR easement legal sufficiency
issues.why: Court must consider whether the DNR-to-MSCA easement complies with statutory and public-trust constraints.

issues.label: Separation of powers concerns
issues.why: Court must assess whether PSC approval improperly intrudes on executive/legislative functions or vice versa.

issues.label: Contractual commitments’ effect
issues.why: Court must decide whether Enbridge–State/MSCA agreements improperly predetermined PSC outcomes or constrained discretion.

issues.label: Conditioning and enforceability
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether PSC conditions are lawful, sufficiently definite, and enforceable.

issues.label: Tunnel ownership and lease issues
issues.why: Court must consider legal implications of MSCA ownership and a 99-year lease for regulatory jurisdiction and obligations.

issues.label: Third-party utilities denial
issues.why: Court must assess whether PSC correctly denied co-location based on evidentiary and safety standards.

issues.label: Segmentation of project review
issues.why: Court must decide whether PSC improperly segmented review of the tunnel, pipeline, and related infrastructure/operations.

issues.label: Cumulative impacts consideration
issues.why: Court must determine whether law required assessment of cumulative/indirect impacts beyond immediate construction footprint.

issues.label: Construction impacts under Straits
issues.why: Court must address environmental/geologic risks from drilling, tunneling, spoil, and potential releases during construction.

issues.label: Operational risk in tunnel
issues.why: Court must evaluate ongoing risks of a tunnel-contained pipeline (leaks, detection, ventilation, emergency response).

issues.label: Emergency response adequacy
issues.why: Court must determine whether PSC properly considered response capabilities and mitigation if a release occurs.

issues.label: Decommissioning obligations
issues.why: Court must consider enforceability and timing of commitments to deactivate the dual pipelines once operational.

issues.label: Interim risk management
issues.why: Court must decide whether PSC had to address risks during the period before replacement is operational.

issues.label: Climate and emissions relevance
issues.why: Court must determine whether greenhouse-gas and climate impacts are legally relevant to PSC’s decision under applicable law.

issues.label: Economic impacts and balancing
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether PSC properly weighed economic benefits/harms against environmental and safety risks.

issues.label: Local government interests
issues.why: Court must consider any required treatment of impacts on localities, shorelines, and regional economies.

issues.label: Evidentiary treatment of experts
issues.why: Court must decide whether PSC properly admitted, weighed, and explained competing expert testimony.

issues.label: Reasoned decision explanation
issues.why: Court must ensure PSC articulated a rational connection between evidence and conclusions on disputed issues.

issues.label: Bias or improper influence
issues.why: Court must consider claims that political negotiations or external pressures compromised agency neutrality.

issues.label: Remedy and scope of relief
issues.why: Court must decide what relief is legally available (vacatur, remand, injunction, conditions) if errors are found.

issues.label: Harmless error doctrine
issues.why: Court must determine whether any procedural or analytical errors require reversal or are harmless.

issues.label: Attorney fees and costs
issues.why: Court must address any statutory or equitable basis for fees/costs (including under MEPA) if requested.

issues.label: Timing and stay standards
issues.why: Court must consider whether to stay construction pending review and the governing criteria for a stay.

issues.label: Interplay with other permits
issues.why: Court must decide how outstanding or parallel state/federal permits affect legality, ripeness, or conditions of PSC approval.

issues.label: Conflicts with other litigation
issues.why: Court must consider coordination/preclusion issues with related Line 5 suits in state or federal courts.

issues.label: Res judicata/collateral estoppel
issues.why: Court must determine whether prior judgments (including Lakehead v Dehn or other Line 5 cases) preclude issues or claims.

issues.label: Statute of limitations/filing deadlines
issues.why: Court must confirm the appeal was timely and complies with jurisdictional deadlines for PSC review.

issues.label: Interpretation of PSC enabling statutes
issues.why: Court must interpret any ambiguous statutory terms governing pipelines/utilities and apply them to a tunnel-based replacement.

issues.label: Classification as public utility
issues.why: Court must determine whether Enbridge/Line 5 is treated as a public utility/common carrier for purposes of PSC authority.

issues.label: Eminent domain implications
issues.why: Court must address whether approvals implicate condemnation authority and whether the project serves a public use.

issues.label: Cross-border regulatory comity
issues.why: Court must consider implications of Canadian delivery and international coordination where relevant to state authority.

issues.label: Environmental justice relevance
issues.why: Court must determine whether any law requires consideration of disproportionate impacts on specific communities/Tribes.

issues.label: Disclosure and transparency
issues.why: Court must assess compliance with disclosure rules (ex parte limits, record evidence, public access) in the PSC process.

issues.label: Interpretation of tunnel safety findings
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether PSC’s safety findings about a concrete-lined tunnel are legally and factually supported.

issues.label: Effect of declining utility co-location
issues.why: Court must determine whether removing third-party utilities changes project purpose, feasibility, or statutory justification.

issues.label: Whether approval is conditional
issues.why: Court must decide if PSC approval was contingent on future events and whether conditions were lawful and sufficiently specific.

issues.label: Agency coordination duties
issues.why: Court must consider whether PSC had duties to coordinate with DNR/MSCA or environmental agencies and whether it did so.

issues.label: Public participation adequacy
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether hearing process allowed meaningful public input given the project’s magnitude.

issues.label: Record-based MEPA alternatives proof
issues.why: Court must decide whether challengers met MEPA’s prima facie showing and whether Enbridge rebutted with no feasible/prudent alternative.

issues.label: Definition of feasible and prudent
issues.why: Court must apply the correct legal meaning of ‘feasible and prudent’ alternatives under Michigan MEPA precedent.

issues.label: Mitigation measures sufficiency
issues.why: Court must determine whether imposed/required mitigation is adequate and legally required to minimize harm.

issues.label: Balancing of tunnel vs shutdown
issues.why: Court must assess whether PSC properly handled the central comparison between replacement and cessation of Straits crossing.
